The '''1999–2000 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 98th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 68th in a [[round-robin tournament]]. It was contested by 18 teams.

By late March, [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] topped the table by nine points over [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] with only eight games remaining, but they lost to [[AC Milan|Milan]], to Lazio at the [[Stadio delle Alpi]], and to [[Hellas Verona FC|Hellas Verona]], with Lazio only dropping two points, against [[AC Fiorentina|Fiorentina]].<ref name="Blair Newman">{{cite news|last1=Newman|first1=Blair|title=How Sven-Goran Eriksson's Lazio won the great Serie A title race of 1999-2000|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/these-football-times/2015/mar/30/sven-goran-eriksson-lazio-serie-a-1999-2000-mancini-milan|access-date=25 February 2017|work=The Guardian|date=30 March 2015}}</ref> Lazio won the title on the final day of the season when Juventus lost their match against [[AC Perugia Calcio|Perugia]] 1–0 on an almost flooded pitch, while Lazio comfortably beat [[Reggina Calcio|Reggina]] 3–0 at home at the [[Stadio Olimpico]].<ref name="Blair Newman"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/rugby-union/49984919 |title=Typhoon Hagibis: When the weather changed a sporting result |first=Ben |last=Sutherland |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 October 2019 |access-date=9 October 2019}}</ref>

==Teams==
[[Image:Italian Serie A 1999-2000 map.svg|thumb|Serie A 1999-2000 team distribution]]
[[Hellas Verona FC|Hellas Verona]], [[Torino FC|Torino]], [[US Lecce|Lecce]] and [[Reggina Calcio|Reggina]] had been promoted from [[Serie B]].
